sentences.text: Ravi vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 April, 2024
High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur
Mcrc No. 2279 of 2024

Ravi S/o Ramsingh Gautam Aged About 23 Years
 R/o Uttam Nagar Bindapur,p.S Bindapur ,district Dwarika West
 Delhi
 ---- Applicant(in 
 Versus
  State Of Chhattisgarh Through P.S. - Cyber Range Bilaspur,
 District : Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh
 ---- Respond
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
For Applicant : Mr. Sanjay Agrawal, Advocate.
For Respondent/State : Mr. Pramod Shrivastava, Dy. Govt.
Advocate.
S.B.:Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu Order On Board 16/04/2024

1 .  This is first bail application filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 on behalf of the applicant for grant of regular bail to him as he is in custody in connection with Crime No.03/2023 registered at Police Station Cyber Range Bilaspur, District Bilaspur (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 66(D), 43 of the Information Technology Act.

2. Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that complainant lodged report in the concerned police-station alleging that she received whatsapp message from Mobile No.447833885923 of Dr. Samesh Nath through matrimonial site 'Shaadi.com' to the effect that he wanted to open a clinic in India and while stating his plan to celebrate his birthday in India, asked the complainant to deposit Rs.25000/- in Indian currency, which he needed for insurance to book a flight.
The complainant deposited the said amount through phone-pay in the bank account of person concerned as requested.
Thereafter, on different dates, the complainant has deposited a total sum of Rs.20,86,200/- at the instance of said Dr. Samesh Nath.

After realizing that she was being cheated,
complainant lodged report in concerned police-station based on which aforementioned crime was registered and during course of investigation, applicant was arrested on 18.10.2023.

Ravi vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125931340/
1 3.
Learned counsel for applicant would submit that applicant has been falsely implicated in instant crime.
He has not committed any offence as alleged.
There is no connecting material available in the case diary/ charge-sheet.

Other two persons namely Harpreet Kaur and Samjhana @ Simran Kaur from whom the police seized ATM card and in whose bank account amount was deposited, have been left over by the police after recording their memorandum statement Applicant is in jail since 18.10.2023, hence, he may be enlarged on regular bail.
4. Learned counsel for the State opposes submissions of learned counsel for applicant and submits that the applicant along with other co-accused persons have committed serious offence and have obtained huge amount of Rs.20,86,200/- through online cheating.
He also contended that the charge-sheet has been filed against Harpreet Kaur, Samjhana @ Simran Kaur and present applicant under Section 173(8) of CrPC.
Other co-accused persons are being traced and against them the matter is still under investigation.

He also submits that in the memorandum statement of co-accused it has come that it is the applicant who approached him for opening the account and handing over the amount to be transferred in their account and in lieu thereof they will be paid commission.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

6. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of case, nature of allegations, manner in which the offence is committed i.e. through online cheating, I do not find present to be a fit case to allow bail application of this applicant.
7. Accordingly, bail application filed under Section 439 of CrPC is rejected.

Sd/-
 (Parth Prateem Sahu)
